section_summary: The section opens with Panama newspaper coverage of the Japanese training cruisers Iwate and Yakumo in May 1933. Reports of receptions, inspections and military reviews appear alongside criticism of Japan’s actions in China and allegations of espionage on the Isthmus. Later records describe the squadron’s reception in Hawaii and the United States, then turn to a 1934–1935 dispute over the treatment of Japanese naval tankers in American ports.

subfiles.title: Japanese admiral lauds Teddy Roosevelt and praises Panama Canal
subfiles.from: J. Preston Crews, The Panama American
subfiles.about: Reports a banquet for Hyakutake and the Iwate and Yakumo officers.
subfiles.summary: Wakabayashi praised Roosevelt and the Panama Canal; Hyakutake described the squadron’s training and goodwill mission.

subfiles.title: Claims Japan is menace to world peace
subfiles.about: Reports a Chinese Legation secretary’s lecture at Balboa High School.
subfiles.summary: Liao denounced Japan’s invasion of China.

subfiles.title: Japanese spokesman talks of courtesies shown group
subfiles.from: J. Preston Crews, The Panama American
subfiles.about: Interviews Ryuzaki and describes the squadron’s Panama itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Ryuzaki praised receptions in U.S. ports and discussed peace and Manchuria; the article lists local visits and entertainment.

subfiles.title: Persiflage: Free Talk About a Banquet
subfiles.about: Criticizes educators and officials for honoring Japanese naval officers amid war in China.
subfiles.summary: The columnist condemns the banquet as lending prestige to Japan’s military.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Peru and Japan
subfiles.about: Contrasts the reception of Japanese cruisers with the treatment of a Peruvian cruiser.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell argues that honoring Japanese officers disregards Chinese suffering and applies a different standard from that used for Peru.

subfiles.title: Why the Kow-Towing
subfiles.about: Questions the unusually elaborate reception for the Japanese squadron.
subfiles.summary: The writer asks why honors exceed those of an earlier visit.

subfiles.title: 250 Japanese see Coco Solo Navy station
subfiles.from: J. Preston Crews, The Panama American
subfiles.about: Describes a squadron visit to the Fleet Air Base and submarine base.
subfiles.summary: Officers and midshipmen inspected Coco Solo facilities and were entertained in Colón.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: T. Tahara
subfiles.about: Accuses Japanese steamship representative T. Tahara of directing an espionage network.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell alleges that Tahara gathered information on Isthmian defenses through local contacts; these are the columnist’s accusations.

subfiles.title: Visiting Japanese navy officers taken on tour of Madden Dam
subfiles.from: J. Preston Crews, The Panama American
subfiles.about: Reports the Madden Dam tour and tension after Rounsevell’s allegations.
subfiles.summary: A reporter accompanied the Japanese party despite apparent discomfort over the preceding column; Hyakutake’s group inspected Madden Dam.

subfiles.title: Japan and U.S. relations better now than ever, admiral says
subfiles.about: Presents Hyakutake’s views on U.S.–Japan relations and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Hyakutake rejected talk of war, defended Japan’s actions in Manchuria and outlined the squadron’s return route.

subfiles.title: Chinese Legation spokesman answers Japanese admiral
subfiles.about: Publishes a Chinese Legation rebuttal of Hyakutake’s interview.
subfiles.summary: The unnamed spokesman rejects Japan’s account of Manchukuo and condemns its campaign in China.

subfiles.title: 3,500 American soldiers pass in review as tribute to Japanese admiral
subfiles.from: J. Preston Crews, The Panama American
subfiles.about: Describes the Fort Amador review and final receptions for the squadron.
subfiles.summary: U.S. troops paraded before Hyakutake and other officers; the Japanese ships prepared to depart for Mexico and Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Fort Amador review
subfiles.about: Explains Rounsevell’s absence from the military review and renews his criticism of the reception.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell recalls wartime service, calls the ceremonial welcome hypocritical, and repeats allegations about Tahara and Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Japanese admiral and vessels leave for homeland
subfiles.about: Reports the Iwate and Yakumo departing Balboa.
subfiles.summary: Bands exchanged anthems and farewells; U.S. officers praised their visitors.

subfiles.title: Japs Getting Bolder
subfiles.about: Makes further allegations about Tahara and Japanese barbershops.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell alleges late-night meetings and document deliveries; the claims are unverified in this clipping.

subfiles.title: The Threat of the East
subfiles.about: Warns of an alleged Japanese military threat and urges Anglo-American cooperation.
subfiles.summary: A letter introduces Zeus’s article, published in the May 22 paper. The article alleges secret Japanese weapons and plans for expansion, and argues for a U.S.–British alliance.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Hawaii entertainment
subfiles.about: Introduces an Army report on the squadron’s Hawaii visit.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the report describes entertainment for Iwate and Yakumo.

subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Division distribution sheet
subfiles.about: Lists recipients for circulation of the attached report.
subfiles.summary: Distribution and filing form.

subfiles.title: Entertainment of Iwate and Yakumo at Schofield Barracks
subfiles.about: Reports receptions and tours for Japanese naval visitors in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Hyakutake’s senior party received honors and luncheon; junior officers and midshipmen toured the post and Wheeler Field.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Japanese cruise address
subfiles.about: Introduces extracts from a Japanese captain’s address.
subfiles.summary: Notes favorable impressions of U.S. hospitality and navy-yard access.

subfiles.title: Cruise of the Japanese Training Squadron
subfiles.doc_type: naval attaché report with speech extracts
subfiles.about: Transmits Captain Niimi’s account of the 1933 squadron cruise.
subfiles.summary: Niimi describes cordial receptions, access to U.S. naval facilities, the Panama Canal visit and the return through Pacific islands. The attaché contrasts American access for visitors with Japanese restrictions.

subfiles.title: Status of Japanese tankers operated by the Japanese Ministry of Marine
subfiles.from: Sidney Browne, American Consulate General, Batavia
subfiles.about: Forwards a Netherlands East Indies inquiry about Japanese naval tankers in California ports.
subfiles.summary: Browne asks for prompt guidance on whether the tankers receive warship privileges under port rules.

subfiles.title: Treatment of Japanese naval tankers in Californian ports
subfiles.from: Coster, Chief of Naval Staff in Netherlands East Indies
subfiles.about: Requests information on Japanese tankers’ port status.
subfiles.summary: Asks about prior notice, pilotage and harbor dues, and lists nine tankers.

subfiles.title: State Department request to Commerce
subfiles.about: Seeks information on pilotage and harbor dues for Japanese naval tankers.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Batavia inquiry to Commerce.

subfiles.title: State Department request to Navy
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japanese tanker visits require diplomatic notice.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Batavia inquiry to Navy.

subfiles.title: State Department request to Treasury
subfiles.about: Asks about quarantine treatment and fees for Japanese tankers.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Batavia inquiry to Treasury.

subfiles.title: Reply to American Consul General at Batavia
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the tanker inquiry and sends departmental replies.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Commerce, Treasury and Navy letters.

subfiles.title: Navy letter on armed Japanese tankers
subfiles.about: Reports armed Japanese tankers entering U.S. ports without diplomatic notice.
subfiles.summary: Cites Tsurumi and Naruto visits and asks that established notice practice be enforced.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.from: William Phillips, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Navy’s report on unannounced armed tanker visits.
subfiles.summary: Says the Japanese ambassador is being informed.

subfiles.title: Information for American Ambassador in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends the Navy letter and note to Japan for the ambassador’s information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses copies concerning unannounced tanker visits.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum to Phillips
subfiles.about: Recommends raising unannounced armed tanker visits with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Supports Navy’s objection and attaches a draft Embassy note.

subfiles.title: Note to Japanese Ambassador on armed tanker visits
subfiles.about: Requests prior diplomatic notification for Japanese public vessels visiting U.S. ports.
subfiles.summary: Names Tsurumi and Naruto visits to Honolulu and San Pedro and cites their guns. The note excepts Philippine ports covered by an informal arrangement.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on quarantine of naval tankers
subfiles.from: Josephine Roche, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Explains quarantine treatment of unarmed foreign naval fuel and supply ships.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says these vessels receive commercial-vessel quarantine treatment and charges; armed vessels on courtesy visits receive nominal supervision.

subfiles.title: Navy reply on notification for unarmed Japanese tankers
subfiles.from: W. H. Standley, Acting Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Explains notice requirements and the limited Philippine Islands arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Navy says the arrangement does not cover mainland U.S. ports and recounts how notifications stopped after 1932.

subfiles.title: Commerce reply on tanker fees and dues
subfiles.about: Explains federal treatment of Japanese naval tankers arriving for fuel.
subfiles.summary: Commerce says fuel calls incur no federal navigation or tonnage fees; commercial cargo changes that treatment. State pilotage and some harbor dues remain outside its answer.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note to Southgate
subfiles.about: Circulates conversation memoranda on a proposed public-vessel arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Notes Navy is reviewing Japanese suggestions.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Kawahara on Japanese public vessels
subfiles.about: Records a discussion of notice rules for Japanese tankers entering American ports.
subfiles.summary: Kawahara claimed earlier understandings allowed local notice. Dooman cited a 1931 memorandum limiting the arrangement to Philippine ports and Navy records showing notifications ceased after 1932. Kawahara proposed extending the arrangement to U.S. ports.

subfiles.title: Copy of note to Japanese Ambassador on armed tanker visits
subfiles.about: Repeats the request for diplomatic notice of Japanese public-vessel visits.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the February 18 note; page 172 ends in damaged OCR.
